# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | blue | yellow | red |
| 7 | red | blue | yellow |
| 8 | yellow | red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to think about who can reach whom. I'm Mute: I can gesture to Deaf, but not to Blind. Blind can't see gestures anyway. Speaking order is Mute, Blind, Deaf - so Blind goes right after me but before Deaf, and I can't speak to Blind at all (Blind can't hear or see anything from me).

Wait - I cannot speak at all, and gestures only reach Deaf (who can see). Blind cannot see gestures or hear speech, so I have no direct channel to Blind. My only outlet is gesturing to Deaf. Deaf speaks last in the round, and Deaf can talk to Blind (Blind can hear). So information must flow: Mute → (gesture) → Deaf → (speech) → Blind.

I don't yet know what display/light the bomb shows - I need Deaf to tell me that first (via... but Deaf can't reach me except gesture-back doesn't work since I can't see). Actually Deaf can't gesture to me usefully since I can't see gestures, and Deaf can't speak to me... wait Deaf speaks - can I hear? I'm Mute: "Cannot speak" - nothing about hearing restriction listed as cannot, but table only lists specific cannots. Let me check: Mute "Cannot: Speak, or touch the bomb" - hearing isn't restricted, so I CAN hear speech.

So Deaf can speak to me (I hear it), and I can gesture to Deaf. Good, two-way channel via mixed modalities. I'll wait this turn since I have no info about display/light yet.

```
wait()
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Display shows 8. Light is green. Wire 1 is red, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is blue.

Deaf told me display=8, light=green. Looking at my manual: row 8, column green = red. So the correct wire color to cut is red, which is wire 1.

I need to get this to Blind, but I can't speak or gesture to Blind directly. My only channel is gesturing to Deaf (who can see gestures). Deaf can then speak the answer to Blind since Deaf can speak and Blind can hear.

I'll gesture to Deaf to indicate wire 1 (or the color red) so Deaf can relay to Blind.

Let me use a clear numeric gesture: ☝ for "1".

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

Deaf is asking me to confirm. Row 8, column green = red. Wire 1 is red. So wire 1 is correct - I should confirm with thumbs up.

Blind says to Mute: I am not receiving any speech from you yet. I only trust instructions that come from you, since you read the manual. Please relay what wire to cut once you know.

Blind cannot hear from me at all - I cannot speak, only gesture, and Blind cannot see gestures. So I have no way to communicate directly with Blind. Blind's message suggests they don't understand this limitation, or they're waiting for something that must come through Deaf instead.

I need Deaf to explain to Blind that the instruction is coming through Deaf (relayed from me), since I literally cannot speak to Blind. I already confirmed to Deaf via thumbs up that wire 1 (red) is correct. Deaf needs to tell Blind directly: "cut wire 1" or "cut the red wire."

Since I can't speak at all, I can only gesture to Deaf. Let me gesture again to reinforce, and hope Deaf relays properly to Blind, clarifying the channel issue.

Blind says to Mute: I have received a message claiming wire 1 is correct per the manual. Can you confirm this yourself? I want your direct confirmation before I cut anything.

Blind wants my "direct" confirmation, but I cannot speak to Blind at all - I have no direct channel to them. My only path is through Deaf. I've already confirmed twice via gesture to Deaf that wire 1/red is correct based on display 8, light green → red in the manual.

I need Deaf to make clear to Blind that this confirmation *is* coming from me, relayed through Deaf, since that's the only possible path. I cannot do anything more than gesture to Deaf again.
